item.text: The current map holds opaque `maphash.Seed` values, which can be regenerated randomly but cannot be set from a caller’s string. I found the hasher is also used by SQLite’s seeded random function, so I’m checking that call path before choosing the representation and adding the regression test.

item.text: The new regression test fails at compile time exactly where expected: neither the instance nor the package exposes `SetSeed`. I’ll store the supplied seed text per ID and keep one `maphash` seed on the `Hasher`, so restoring a seed repeats the same hash within the running instance.

The targeted regression now passes. The implementation also guards the per-ID seed map because SQLite can invoke the hash callback through multiple connections; I’m finishing the race check and the repository’s persistence/database tests before wrapping up.

Added per-ID `SetSeed` to the exported `Hasher` and the package API. Setting a seed now produces repeatable hashes for that identifier; reseeding changes them, and restoring the seed restores the original results. First use still initializes a seed automatically.

Regression tests and the existing hasher, persistence, and database tests pass. The hasher race check also passes. Hash values remain stable within a running `Hasher`; its global `maphash` seed is regenerated when a new instance is created.
